set.approach: Parties camp on the glacier at the foot of Mt. Huntington's west face and start from there. Cross the lower glacier, where crevasse navigation is needed, to the bergschrund that guards the Access Couloir at the foot of the face; the crossing can be awkward. Register with the Denali National Park mountaineering office in Talkeetna before climbing.
set.descent_text: From the summit, reverse the ridge and start rappelling, first off a bollard and then on V-threads down the ice. Do not retrace the line of ascent: rappel toward the overhanging rock above the head of the West Face Couloir, where fixed anchors lead into the gully. The couloir is descended by a long series of V-thread rappels mixed with some downclimbing, followed by rock anchors lower down. Cross the bergschrund at the bottom and return to the upper basin above camp, taking care among large crevasses.

review.notes: Approach from guide trip page (camp below west face, crevasses, bergschrund into Access Couloir); descent from both pages (V-thread rappels down West Face Couloir). Rappel counts differ (about a dozen vs 20 total) so omitted.

set.approach: The mountain is reached by ski-plane to the Nabesna Glacier in the Wrangell Mountains. From the landing area, the route follows low-angle glaciers, with camps possible nearly anywhere along them, to the foot of the summit pyramid, which is steep technical ice and snow climbed by its southeast ridge.

review.notes: Fly-in to Nabesna Glacier (area page + air service), low-angle glaciers then summit pyramid via SE ridge (route page + air service). No descent source.

set.approach: Access is normally by ski-plane onto the lower Sheep Glacier, though a very long walk in from the highway is possible. From the landing, parties rope up and haul sleds up the glacier to a base camp. The route climbs a glacial ramp through large crevasse fields and a tricky icefall.
set.descent_text: The descent retraces the route down the glacier to the landing area, with the crevasse fields and icefall to negotiate again on the way down.

review.notes: Fly-in or long walk (area page); lower Sheep Glacier landing, sleds, ramp, crevasses, icefall, reverse route (guide page).

set.approach: The Munchkin sits in the middle of Little Switzerland and is a short ski from the base camp on the Pika Glacier. The route faces generally south and is mixed snow and rock with broken ledges up to a boulder on the summit ridge.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappel: one anchor on a boulder drops you to the snow bench, and a second anchor above the gully gets you back down to where skis or snowshoes were left.

review.notes: Short ski from Pika base camp (area page); raps from route page.

set.descent_text: Slings placed near the top let parties rappel the route.

review.notes: Only descent statement is the slings near the top allowing a rappel descent of the route; approach not described beyond a drainage camp, so omitted.

set.approach: Start at the Glen Alps trailhead and follow the Powerline Trail away from town, on foot or skis, to an obvious side trail on the left. Follow it down and over the creek, then either cross the field or take the Williwaw Creek trail, and continue to the north side of O'Malley Peak. The falls hang above the Williwaw Lakes. Some approach options cross serious avalanche terrain and the route itself lies in an avalanche path, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Parties rappel the route. A fixed anchor of old pitons at a prominent rock formation near the top is the first station, and further rappels need V-threads because alders are sparse. A walk-off is also possible from the top of the last pitch.

review.notes: Approach from both pages (Glen Alps, Powerline, Williwaw, north side, above lakes); avalanche note from route page; descent: V-threads both pages, pitons and walk-off route page only.

set.approach: Peak 11,300 lies beside the West Fork of the Ruth Glacier, a little north of Mt. Huntington; parties usually start from the usual landing spots in the Ruth Gorge. The route starts on a steep snow and ice face that leads into an ice couloir, with a natural ice cave near the top of the couloir.

review.notes: Area and route pages; descent not stated for this line.

set.approach: Peak 11,300 lies beside the West Fork of the Ruth Glacier, a little north of Mt. Huntington; parties usually start from the usual landing spots in the Ruth Gorge. The couloir is on the west face, a short ski up the glacier beyond the southwest ridge. The first mixed section can be bypassed by walking up the couloir on its left.
set.descent_text: Parties can rappel the line and skip the ridge traverse, or carry on to the summit and come down the standard route.

review.notes: Area and route page.

set.approach: The lower approach crosses glaciated ground, so rope up and carry crevasse rescue gear. The route starts from the small pocket northeast of Crosson and follows the southwest ridge, picking the easiest line between loose scree and snow slopes.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.approach: From the Glen Alps trailhead, follow the Powerline Trail up the valley, on skis or by bike in winter, until the largest peak on the right-hand ridge comes into view; the north couloir, a broad snow gully splitting the north face, is the landmark. The route is the prominent ice drip that overhangs the north couloir, well up inside it. Climb the couloir to reach it. The terrain is avalanche-prone in winter, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Shared approach from two pages; route location from its own page; no descent stated.

set.approach: From the Glen Alps trailhead, follow the Powerline Trail up the valley, on skis or by bike in winter, until the largest peak on the right-hand ridge comes into view; the north couloir, a broad snow gully splitting the north face, is the landmark. The route is on the tallest, steepest cliff on the side of the north couloir. Climb the couloir to its base. The terrain is avalanche-prone in winter, so check the avalanche forecast.

The route follows the obvious corner just right of El Shaddai, on the cliff beside the north couloir. Climb the couloir to its base. The terrain is avalanche-prone in winter, so check the avalanche forecast.

set.approach: From the Glen Alps trailhead, follow the Powerline Trail up the valley, on skis or by bike in winter, until the largest peak on the right-hand ridge comes into view; the north couloir, a broad snow gully splitting the north face, is the landmark. The route starts from the ledge system right of 32 and Beautiful and is close to the left-hand exits of Mixed Inhibitions. Reach the ledge from the north couloir. The terrain is avalanche-prone in winter, so check the avalanche forecast.

set.approach: From the Glen Alps trailhead, follow the Powerline Trail up the valley, on skis or by bike in winter, until the largest peak on the right-hand ridge comes into view; the north couloir, a broad snow gully splitting the north face, is the landmark. The route starts about 200 feet higher in the couloir than Ski Tracks; a large chockstone on the line is visible from below and helps to locate it. The terrain is avalanche-prone in winter, so check the avalanche forecast.

set.approach: From the Glen Alps trailhead, follow the Powerline Trail up the valley, on skis or by bike in winter, until the largest peak on the right-hand ridge comes into view; the north couloir, a broad snow gully splitting the north face, is the landmark. Ski Tracks lies right of the main snow gully and right of the Hookers line. The terrain is avalanche-prone, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Descend the north couloir, or drop down the south side toward Ptarmigan Pass and traverse back around to the base.

review.notes: Approach: both listings + AIC route page; descent: route page only.

set.approach: This line is not on the Roctober wall. Cross the lake that leads toward that wall and look high and right on the flank of Ptarmigan for a thin smear of ice; the climb begins at an icy break to the left of a large chockstone roof.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. Slings and fixed anchors are in place at the third and fourth pitches.

review.notes: Single route page.

set.descent_text: The ice is short enough to top-rope, and parties can also walk off.

review.notes: Single route page; approach not stated beyond east side above Green Lake.

set.approach: Park at the Gold Rush cemetery in Skagway and walk the cemetery path to the falls; it is a short stroll. The base is reached by soloing an easy WI2 ramp.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted anchor at the top of the ice. If you would rather not downclimb the easy ramp at the base, add a short rappel there.

review.notes: Cemetery trail from both pages; ramp and rappel from route page.

set.approach: From the airstrip and base camp on the Pika Glacier, ski or snowshoe west to the foot of the Royal Tower. Depending on the line you may need an ice axe and crampons for steep snow and a bergschrund crossing. The line is the middle couloir of the north face.
set.descent_text: Rappel to the couloir, which can then be downclimbed or rappelled.

review.notes: Area approach; route page for couloir and descent.

set.approach: From the airstrip and base camp on the Pika Glacier, ski or snowshoe west to the foot of the Royal Tower. Depending on the line you may need an ice axe and crampons for steep snow and a bergschrund crossing. The line is the more easterly of two side-by-side gully systems, next to Boomerang Buttress.

review.notes: Area approach; route page for couloir; descent not stated.

set.approach: Access is by ski-plane to the Nabesna Glacier. A base camp can be set among crevasses that give some protection from avalanches off the neighbouring peak, and a higher camp can go on the saddle that links Ahtna with Rime Peak. Expect steep snow on the north face broken by a short band or two of alpine ice, and falling ice from seracs is a hazard.

review.notes: Fly-in (3 pages), camps and hazards (route page + air service).

set.approach: Park near the highway bridge with the cabins and walk along the river to the Goat Trail and Wagon Road, an easy track that runs just below the climbs. The gulch is avalanche-prone, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Area approach; descent not stated.

set.approach: Start from the Caines Head trailhead at Lowell Point State Recreation Area near Seward and follow the trail to the broken bridge over Tonsina Creek, then hike the main Tonsina Creek drainage upstream to where the river forks in a clear Y. Take the left branch briefly, then duck left into a small alcove; the pillar stays hidden until you round a short hill.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from a V-thread.

review.notes: Single detailed page for the Y-split; distances disagree so omitted.

set.approach: Follow the Caines Head trail from Lowell Point to the broken bridge over Tonsina Creek, then continue up the drainage; the route is on the north side. The approach, which passes through a slot canyon, snow and brush, can be one of the cruxes.
set.descent_text: Alders and natural gear are available for the descent.

review.notes: Single route page for specifics.

set.approach: Follow the Caines Head trail from Lowell Point to the broken bridge over Tonsina Creek, then continue up the drainage on the north side. A snow gully through trees leads to the base of a steep ice pillar. The approach can be one of the cruxes.

review.notes: Single route page for specifics.

set.approach: The tower is across the gorge from Mt. Bradley and Mt. Wake, and the approach is easy. Watch for crevasses near the end. The route is the couloir in the slot between London Tower and Werewolf Tower.
set.descent_text: Descend by a mix of downclimbing and rappelling from the stations on the route; carry extra cord to reinforce them. Most parties stop at the col between the two towers.

review.notes: Route page and area page.

set.approach: The wall is in Suicide Basin and is reached either on foot via the West Glacier trail and across the Mendenhall Glacier, or by a short helicopter ride from Juneau. The approach passes beneath the Suicide icefall, so move quickly there.

review.notes: Approach from both; descent V-thread from AIC.

set.approach: The wall is in Suicide Basin and is reached either on foot via the West Glacier trail and across the Mendenhall Glacier, or by a short helicopter ride from Juneau. The Suicide icefall is to the left of the route, and a big gentle slope lies higher up.

review.notes: Approach from both; descent from AIC.
